'''Earl Rashad Clark''' (born January 17, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Club Atlético Aguada]] of the [[Liga Uruguaya de Básquetbol]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Louisville]] and was drafted 14th overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Clark grew up in [[Plainfield, New Jersey]] and attended [[Rahway High School]] in [[Rahway, New Jersey]]. There, he scored 1,245 career points.  As a senior, he averaged 25.2 points, 13.2 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He was a 2006 [[McDonald's All-American]], as well as a fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uoflsports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/clark_earl00.html |title=Louisville bio |work=UOfLSports.CSTV.com |access-date=January 2, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090221233830/http://uoflsports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/clark_earl00.html |archive-date=February 21, 2009 }}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Clark was listed as the No. 8 small forward and the No. 22 player in the nation in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Earl-Clark-30653;_ylt=Ao0qtlIIyvyHXQhjqrni4MFGPZB4|title=Earl Clark Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=March 15, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]], along with [[Derrick Caracter]], [[Edgar Sosa (basketball)|Edgar Sosa]], and [[Jerry Smith (basketball, born 1987)|Jerry Smith]], the young group struggled early in the 2006–07 season. The team went on to win 8 out of its last 10 games, earning a bid to the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]].

In the first game of the 2007 NCAA Tournament, he scored 12 points, 4 rebounds and 4 steals against [[Stanford]].

Clark decided not to put his name in the 2008 NBA Draft and to return to the University of Louisville for the 2008–2009 season.

In the 2008–2009 season, Clark, along with future NBA player [[Terrence Williams]], led Louisville to the Big East Title, as well as a #1 ranking, the first ever in the University of Louisville's history.

==Professional career==
===Phoenix Suns (2009–2010)===
Early in his junior season, Clark announced that he would forgo his senior season to enter the [[2009 NBA draft]].  On April 4, 2009, [[sports agent|agent]] Dan Fegan told [[ESPN]] that he had signed Clark as a client shortly after the end of Louisville's [[2008–09 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2008–09 season]], which under NCAA rules ended Clark's college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=InOut|title=Who's in, who's out of 2009 draft?|first=Chad|last=Ford|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2009|access-date=April 1, 2009}}</ref>

Clark was drafted 14th overall by the Phoenix Suns in the [[2009 NBA draft]].<ref>Coro, Paul (June 26, 2009). – "A new look in the works". – ''[[The Arizona Republic]]''.</ref> He made his first career three pointer on January 28, 2010. Clark was sent to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on March 15, 2010, after only averaging 2.7 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 7.6 minutes in 45 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2010/03/15/earl-clark-sent-down-to-d-league/|title=Earl Clark sent down to D-League|work=NBCSports.com|date=March 15, 2010|access-date=March 15, 2010}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2010–2012)===
[[File:John Wall and Earl Clark.jpg|thumb|right|Clark battling with [[John Wall]] in 2011]]
On December 18, 2010, Clark was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] along with [[Jason Richardson]] and [[Hedo Türkoğlu]] for [[Vince Carter]], [[Marcin Gortat]], [[Mickaël Piétrus]], a [[2011 NBA draft|2011]] first-round draft pick and $3 million cash.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_sunsdeal_121810.html|title=Magic Receive Turkoglu, Richardson & Clark From Suns|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2010|access-date=December 18, 2010}}</ref> On April 16, 2012, he recorded his first [[double-double]] with 14 points and 11 rebounds.

In August 2011 during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Clark signed a one-year contract with [[Zhejiang Lions]] in China.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/87965/earl-clark-heading-to-zhejiang-in-china.html|title=Earl Clark heading to Zhejiang in China|work=Sportando|date=August 10, 2011|access-date=August 10, 2011}}</ref> However, the next month, he asked to leave the team for family reasons after not appearing in a game for the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2011/09/28/earl-clark-returns-from-china-will-be-an-unrestricted-nba-free-agent/|title=Earl Clark returns from China, will be an unrestricted NBA free agent|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=September 28, 2011|access-date=September 28, 2011}}</ref> He re-signed with Orlando in December.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic_resign_earl_clark_121511.html | title=Magic Re-Sign Earl Clark | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc | date=December 15, 2011 | access-date=December 16, 2011}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2012–2013)===
[[File:Chris Kaman & Earl Clark.jpg|thumb|right|Clark boxed out by [[Chris Kaman]] of the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in a 2013 game]]
On August 10, 2012, Clark was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] as part of a four-team trade that sent [[Dwight Howard]] to the Lakers. The [[Denver Nuggets]] acquired [[Andre Iguodala]], the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] received [[Andrew Bynum]] and [[Jason Richardson]], and the [[Orlando Magic]] got [[Arron Afflalo]], [[Al Harrington]], [[Nikola Vučević]], [[Maurice Harkless]], [[Josh McRoberts]], [[Christian Eyenga]], and one protected future first-round pick from each of the other three teams. The Lakers also acquired [[Chris Duhon]] from the Magic in the trade.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=August 11, 2012 |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/08/10/dwight-howard-trade.ap/index.html |title=It's official: Howard dealt to Lakers in four-team trade |publisher=NBA |date=August 10, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811080542/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/08/10/dwight-howard-trade.ap/index.html |archive-date=August 11, 2012 }}</ref> On January 9, 2013, Clark had a breakthrough night, playing 27 minutes and setting personal bests with 22 points and 13 rebounds against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref name=bresnahan/> He had been playing sparingly, but he received extended playing time after injuries to Lakers big men [[Dwight Howard]], [[Pau Gasol]], and [[Jordan Hill (basketball)|Jordan Hill]].<ref name=mcmenamin_01222013>{{cite news |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |title=Pau Gasol to be reserve for Lakers |date=January 22, 2013 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/8867466/pau-gasol-los-angeles-lakers-come-bench |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130122171117/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/8867466/pau-gasol-los-angeles-lakers-come-bench |archive-date=January 22, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Coach [[Mike D'Antoni]] called Clark's performance "phenomenal"; it was only the second [[double-double]] of Clark's career.<ref name=bresnahan>{{cite news|last=Bresnahan|first=Mike|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/la-sp-lakers-fyi-20130110,0,4505968.story |title=Earl Clark has 'phenomenal' showing for Lakers |date=January 9, 2013|access-date=January 22, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> Clark had three double-doubles over six games, and he was named a permanent starter even after Gasol returned.<ref name=mcmenamin_01222013/>  After three years of limited opportunities, Clark was averaging nearly 30 minutes a game.  However, he appeared tired by March, and D'Antoni replaced Clark with Gasol in the starting lineup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shelburne |first=Ramona |title=Earl Clark slowing down a bit |date=March 9, 2013 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/36059/earl-clark-slowing-down-a-bit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130313073536/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/36059/earl-clark-slowing-down-a-bit |archive-date=March 13, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Pincus |first=Eric |title=Earl Clark is adjusting to return to the bench |date=April 3, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-lakers-earl-clark-20130403,0,454234.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130408055607/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-lakers-earl-clark-20130403,0,454234.story |archive-date=April 8, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2013–2014)===
On July 12, 2013, Clark signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/clark-jack-signing-130712|title=Cavaliers Sign Jack and Clark|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref>

On February 20, 2014, Clark was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] along with [[Henry Sims]] and two future second-round picks in exchange for [[Spencer Hawes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-acquire-two-second-round-picks-2014-nba-draft-cleveland-cavaliers|title=Sixers Acquire Two Second-Round Picks in 2014 NBA Draft From Cleveland Cavaliers|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=February 20, 2014}}</ref> He was waived by the 76ers the next day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140221-clark-waived|title=Sixers Waive Earl Clark|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2014|access-date=February 21, 2014}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2014)===
On February 27, 2014, Clark signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://knicksnow.com/posts/5272/knicks-sign-shannon-brown-earl-clark-to-10-day-contracts |title=Knicks Sign Shannon Brown, Earl Clark To 10-Day Contracts |work=KnicksNow.com |date=February 27, 2014 |access-date=February 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313210342/http://knicksnow.com/posts/5272/knicks-sign-shannon-brown-earl-clark-to-10-day-contracts |archive-date=March 13, 2014 }}</ref> On March 10, 2014, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://knicksnow.com/posts/5369/knicks-sign-earl-clark-and-shannon-brown-to-2nd-10-day-contracts |title=Knicks Sign Earl Clark And Shannon Brown To 2nd 10-Day Contracts |work=KnicksNow.com |date=March 10, 2014 |access-date=March 10, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140910130131/http://knicksnow.com/posts/5369/knicks-sign-earl-clark-and-shannon-brown-to-2nd-10-day-contracts |archive-date=September 10, 2014 }}</ref> On March 20, 2014, the Knicks did not offer him a rest of season contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/232541/Shannon-Brown-Signs-With-Knicks-For-Remainder-Of-Season|title=Shannon Brown Signs With Knicks For Remainder Of Season|work=RealGM.com|date=March 20, 2014|access-date=March 20, 2014}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2014)===
On September 25, 2014, Clark signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/2014-training-camp-roster-140924|title=Memphis Grizzlies announce 2014 Training Camp roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2014|access-date=September 25, 2014}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Grizzlies on October 22, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/grizzlies-waive-clark-whiteside-141022|title=Grizzlies waive Earl Clark and Hassan Whiteside|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2014|access-date=October 22, 2014}}</ref> He was then claimed off waivers by the [[Houston Rockets]] on October 24,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-claim-earl-clark-waivers-and-request-waivers-josh-powell|title=Rockets Claim Earl Clark Off Waivers and Request Waivers on Josh Powell|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014|access-date=October 24, 2014}}</ref> only to be waived again three days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-adrien-clark-covington-richmond-and-smith|title=Rockets Waive Adrien, Clark, Covington, Richmond and Smith|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 27, 2014}}</ref>

On October 31, 2014, Clark was acquired by the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/iowa_energy_announce_returning_2014_10_31.html|title=IOWA ENERGY ANNOUNCE RETURNING, TRYOUT PLAYERS FOR 2014 TRAINING CAMP|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2014|access-date=October 31, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106155156/http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/iowa_energy_announce_returning_2014_10_31.html|archive-date=November 6, 2014}}</ref> However, he was traded to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/201415TrainingCampRoster.html |title=RGV VIPERS SET 2014-15 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |work=NBA.com |date=November 2, 2014 |access-date=November 2, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106214905/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/201415TrainingCampRoster.html |archive-date=November 6, 2014 }}</ref>

===Shandong Golden Stars (2014–2015)===
On December 10, 2014, Clark signed with the [[Shandong Golden Stars]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] after reaching a buyout with the Rio Grande Valley Vipers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/144246/earl-clark-signs-with-shandong-lions.html|title=Earl Clark signs with Shandong Lions|work=Sportando.com|date=December 10, 2014|access-date=December 10, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2014-12-10/10457441770.shtml|title=山东男篮签约湖人旧将 拉杜利察被裁|work=Sina.com.cn|language=zh|date=December 10, 2014|access-date=December 10, 2014}}</ref> In 19 games for Shandong, he averaged 26.7 points and 10.3 rebounds per game.

===Brooklyn Nets (2015)===
On March 27, 2015, Clark signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/earl-clark-10-day-contract|title=Meet 'Eazy' Earl Clark, the Newest Member of the Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150329050722/http://www.nba.com/nets/earl-clark-10-day-contract|archive-date=March 29, 2015}}</ref> On April 6, 2015, he signed a multi-year deal with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/nets-sign-earl-clark-multi-year-contact|title=Nets Sign Earl Clark Multi-Year {{sic|Conta|ct|nolink=y}} |work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2015|access-date=April 6, 2015}}</ref> On August 10, 2015, he was waived by the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-earl-clark|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Earl Clark|work=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2015|access-date=August 10, 2015}}</ref>

===Bakersfield Jam (2015–2016)===
On October 30, 2015, Clark was acquired by the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5066162|title=Jam Announce 2015-16 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 2, 2015|access-date=November 2, 2015}}</ref>

===Delaware 87ers (2016)===
On January 16, 2016, Clark was traded to the [[Delaware 87ers]] in exchange for a 2016 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/bakersfield-jam-complete-two-trades-with-delaware-87ers/n-5090574|title=Bakersfield Jam Complete Two Trades with Delaware 87ers|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 16, 2016|access-date=January 16, 2016}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut for the 87ers in a 127–112 loss to the [[Westchester Knicks]], recording four points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks in 21 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160119/WESDEL/|title=Knicks Rally To Defeat Delaware 87ers|work=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2016|access-date=March 21, 2016|archive-date=February 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160227143744/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160119/WESDEL/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 19, he was waived by Delaware.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Delaware-87ers/36/Transaction_History/2016|title=2015-2016 Delaware 87ers Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=March 21, 2016}}</ref>

=== Beşiktaş (2016–2018) ===
On May 24, 2016, Clark signed with [[Henan Roaring Elephants]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/200278/earl-clark-signs-with-henan-in-china.html|title=Earl Clark signs with Henan in China|work=Sportando.com|date=May 24, 2016|access-date=May 30, 2016}}</ref>

On August 18, 2016, Clark signed with Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Besiktas signs Earl Clark|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/209783/besiktas-signs-earl-clark.html|access-date=August 18, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=August 18, 2016}}</ref> On July 3, 2017, he re-signed with Beşiktaş for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/239708/earl-clark-re-signs-with-besiktas-istanbul.html Earl Clark re-signs with Besiktas Istanbul]</ref> He also made the 2017 BSL All Star Game

===Budućnost VOLI (2018–2019)===
On June 16, 2018, Clark signed with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost VOLI]] of the [[Montenegrin Basketball League]] for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web | title = NOVO POJAČANJE - EARL CLARK | work = [[KK Budućnost]] | date = June 16, 2018 | url = http://www.kkbuducnost.me/clanak274 | access-date = June 17, 2018 | language = hr | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180617165050/http://www.kkbuducnost.me/clanak274 | archive-date = June 17, 2018 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

===San Pablo Burgos (2019–2020)===
On July 19, 2019, Clark signed with Spanish club [[CB Miraflores|San Pablo Burgos]].<ref>{{cite news |title=ACB.COM - El talento de Earl Clark llega al San Pablo Burgos |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=147318 |access-date=July 19, 2019 |work=www.acb.com |date=July 19, 2019 |language=es-ES }}{{Dead link|date=February 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Clark became their "[[franchise player]]",<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2020/05/17/radio_castilla/1589711117_866208.html|website=[[Cadena SER]]|title=El San Pablo al completo menos Clark|first=Jorge|last=Monge|date=May 17, 2020}}</ref> averaging 12.2 points and 5.9 rebounds per game in the Liga ACB. He travelled to the US to be with his family after the ACB league cancellation in the midst of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Having troubles to return to Spain during the lockdown to resume practice sessions,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.solobasket.com/liga-endesa/earl-clark-y-san-pablo-burgos-separan-trayectorias|website=Solobasket|title=Earl Clark y San Pablo Burgos separan trayectorias|first=Rodrigo|last=García|date=May 15, 2020}}</ref> San Pablo Burgos and Clark mutually decided to part ways on May 15, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Earl Clark, San Pablo Burgos part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/earl-clark-san-pablo-burgos-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=May 15, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

=== Anyang KGC (2020) ===
On June 19, 2020, Clark signed with the Korean team [[Anyang KGC]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Anyang KGC tabs Earl Clark and Latavious Williams |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/anyang-kgc-tabs-earl-clark-and-latavious-williams/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 19, 2020 |date=June 19, 2020|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>

=== Gran Canaria (2020–2021) ===
On December 22, 2020, Clark signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/659600/Gran-Canaria-inks-Earl-Clark,-ex-Anyang-KGC|title=Gran Canaria inks Earl Clark, ex Anyang KGC|date=December 22, 2020|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=December 22, 2020}}</ref>

On December 31, 2021, Clark signed with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES EARL CLARK, SAM THOMPSON|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-earl-clark-sam-thompson/|url-status=live|access-date=December 31, 2021|website=Sioux Falls Skyforce|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211231150638/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-earl-clark-sam-thompson/ |archive-date=December 31, 2021 }}</ref> Clark was then later waived on January 21, 2022, without playing a game for the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=January 21, 2022}}</ref>

===NLEX Road Warriors (2022)===
In August 2022, he signed with the [[NLEX Road Warriors]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2022–23 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arangkadanlex.com/2022/08/24/nba-vet-earl-clark-to-reinforce-nlex-in-commissioners-cup/|title=NBA vet Earl Clark to reinforce NLEX in Commissioner's Cup|publisher=Arangkada NLEX|date=August 24, 2022|accessdate=August 24, 2022|archive-date=October 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221009091007/https://arangkadanlex.com/2022/08/24/nba-vet-earl-clark-to-reinforce-nlex-in-commissioners-cup/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Gigantes de Carolina (2023)===
On February 4, 2023, he signed with [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/earl-clark-signs-with-gigantes-de-carolina/|title=Earl Clark signs with Gigantes de Carolina|date=February 4, 2023|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 5, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers (2023–2025)===
On September 13, 2024, Clark re-signed with the [[Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).<ref>{{cite news |title=攻城獅找回前NBA全能前鋒 克拉正式續約洋將全到齊 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2816450 |accessdate=September 13, 2024 |work=ETtoday |date=September 13, 2024 }}</ref> On May 14, 2025, the [[Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers]] announced that Clark left the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=「風城人生」正式落幕 攻城獅宣布洋將克拉離隊 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2960578 |accessdate=May 14, 2025 |work=ETtoday |date=May 14, 2025 }}</ref>
